BiblicalUsage: Rakash is to lay up, to collect — to gather substance. Abram took Sarai and Lot and all their substance that they had gathered, and went forth into the land of Canaan; Jacob took all his cattle and all his goods which he had gotten in Padan-aram; and Israel took his journey with all that he had, and came to Beersheba.
TheologicalSignificance: The lesson I take is that the gathered substance follows the calling: Abram gathered and went, Jacob gathered and returned, and Israel gathered and went down into Egypt — and God went with the gathering.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
